**Experiment programming**

The following repository contains code designed to introduce
the basics of programming behavioural experiments in Python.

- <a href="https://github.com/crossley/crossleylab/tree/main/code/behavioural_experiment_progression" target="_blank">Behavioural experiment progression</a>

This sequence progresses from drawing stimuli and handling
timing and input to implementing state-based control of
behaviour. The scripts demonstrate how input, timing, and
display updates combine to form structured experimental
tasks, culminating in complete behavioural experiments such
as action selection, category learning, and reaching tasks.
Advanced examples demonstrate efficient visual stimulus
generation using NumPy.

---

## Introduction to dynamical systems (weeks 4 - 5)

- <a href="https://github.com/crossley/crossleylab/tree/main/code/electrochemical_signals_progression" target="_blank">Electrochemical signals progression</a>

These scripts progress from numerical integration (Euler’s
method) to particle-based simulations of diffusion across a
membrane, adding selective channels and electrical forces to
illustrate electrochemical gradients. Later examples convert
ion imbalance across a membrane into a simple
resting-potential–like signal, providing a visual and
computational introduction to membrane potentials and
electrochemical signalling.

---

## Models of single neurons (weeks 6 - 7)

- <a href="tutorials/tutorial_6.html" target="_blank">Hodgkin–Huxley neuron</a>

Tutorial 6 develops a detailed understanding of the
Hodgkin–Huxley neuron by implementing the full model,
examining the behaviour of activation and inactivation
gates, and exploring how membrane dynamics change as
biophysical parameters are varied. Students reproduce key
figures to build intuition for how conductances and reversal
potentials shape action potentials, and then investigate how
different current injections produce single spikes or spike
trains. The focus is on understanding how cellular
mechanisms give rise to excitability through simulation and
parameter exploration.

- <a href="tutorials/tutorial_7.html" target="_blank">Izhikevich neuron</a>

Tutorial 7 moves from biophysically detailed models to
simpler dynamical neuron models, focusing on the Izhikevich
and quadratic integrate-and-fire formulations. Students
reproduce canonical firing patterns, analyse oscillatory
behaviour mathematically, and examine conditions under which
simplified models are equivalent to integrate-and-fire
neurons. The emphasis is on connecting dynamical systems
analysis with reduced neuron models used in large-scale
simulations.

- <a href="https://github.com/crossley/crossleylab/tree/main/code/iz_neurons" target="_blank">Izhikevich neuron code repository</a>

These scripts progress from a single-variable leaky membrane
model (Euler updates) to a two-state \(v,u\) system and then
to the quadratic voltage dynamics used in Izhikevich models.
Later examples implement the full threshold-reset
Izhikevich neuron, compare regular-spiking-like and
fast-spiking-like parameter sets, and conclude with a
side-by-side comparison of MSN-like and cortical
pyramidal-like response profiles under matched and
compensated inputs.

## Building networks (week 8)

- <a href="https://github.com/crossley/crossleylab/tree/main/code/basal_ganglia_spiking_network" target="_blank">Basal ganglia spiking network</a>

This repository walks you through a five-step open-loop spiking
basal ganglia tutorial. You begin with the direct pathway, then
add the indirect and hyperdirect pathways, so you can see how
activity propagates from sensory cortex through basal ganglia
output to thalamus and motor cortex. You then examine reciprocal
STN-GPe coupling in both stable and high-gain regimes. The final
lesson introduces dopamine by applying opposite effects to
corticostriatal input efficacy for D1 versus D2 pathways, with
low, baseline, and high dopamine conditions.

Core lessons:

- The direct pathway facilitates behavioral drive by reducing GPi
  output and releasing thalamocortical activity.
- The indirect pathway suppresses behavioral drive by increasing
  inhibitory control over thalamic output.
- The hyperdirect pathway provides a faster inhibitory "brake"
  through cortex -> STN -> GPi.
- The STN-GPe loop regulates overall network gain and stability,
  helping determine whether activity remains controlled or becomes
  exaggerated/oscillatory.
- Dopamine biases action selection by increasing effective
  corticostriatal influence on D1 pathways while decreasing it on
  D2 pathways.


## Synaptic plasticity (weeks 9 - 13)

- <a href="https://github.com/crossley/crossleylab/tree/main/code/basal_ganglia_spiking_network_cat_learn" target="_blank">Basal ganglia spiking network with category learning</a>

This repository introduces learning rules that modify
synaptic strength over time, illustrating how Hebbian
learning shapes connectivity through correlated activity and
how reinforcement learning introduces reward-dependent
plasticity and credit assignment. These ideas are integrated
in a computational model that combines neural dynamics,
network interactions, and learning within a basal ganglia
framework, demonstrating how reinforcement-driven plasticity
can support procedural category learning and providing a
reference model for final projects.
